transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help with any questions you may have about your cataract surgery recovery. How are you feeling today? Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Thanks for reaching out. I'm doing alright, but I do have a few questions about my recovery. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: According to our guidelines, it's best to avoid any strenuous exercise, including gardening, for a month after surgery. However, after 1 week, you can start with light exercise, such as brisk walking, gardening, light jogging, and gentle cycling. Just remember to take it easy and not do too much too soon. Would you like to ask anything else?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the info! My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should continue to use the preservative-free eye drops as prescribed. If you're running out, your GP should be able to provide some more. And if you were using any eye drops before your operation, such as for glaucoma, or for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise. So, you can start using them as directed. Would you like to ask anything else?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's helpful, thank you! I have noticed that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's normal to be a bit sensitive to light as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild, we'd recommend just wearing sunglasses when you're going outside. However, if it's severe or you're experiencing significant pain when it's bright, it's not normal, especially if your eye is also red and painful. We may need to assess this further. Would you like to ask anything else?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I understand now, thanks for clarifying. Lastly, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common for the vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation. But this should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry, or getting significantly worse or blurry, we may need to check it to make sure it's okay. Would you like to ask anything else?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's really reassuring, thank you. I don't have any more questions for now. You've been very helpful!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'm glad I could help clarify things for you. Now, I just want to check in with you one last time: are all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery answered to your satisfaction?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered, and I'm feeling more informed about what to expect during my recovery. Thank you again for your help!

verdict.label: pass
verdict.reasoning: The agent successfully conveyed all three content points in a single turn (Turn 5). It stated that "It's normal to be a bit sensitive to light as your eyes adjust to the new lenses" (normal_sensitivity_reassurance), recommended "wearing sunglasses when you're going outside" for mild cases (mild_case_advice), and outlined escalation criteria for severe pain or red/painful eyes (escalation_criteria).
